description:
## Why this issue exists

Usenet was born on UUCP. The first Usenet article was exchanged via UUCP dial-up between Duke and UNC in 1980. NNTP over TCP did not exist until RFC 977 in 1986. stoa implementing UUCP transport is not retro — it is restoration.

Adding UUCP as a transport layer completes the picture: stoa peers via NNTP/TCP with modern transit nodes and via UUCP with intermittently-connected nodes, ham radio gateways, airgapped systems, and sneakernet. All transports feed the same CID-addressed article store and the same JMAP/IMAP user interface.

## Genuine non-joke use cases

- Ham radio / packet radio store-and-forward (AX.25, Winlink-adjacent)
- HF data links with small, intermittent bandwidth windows
- Crisis communication infrastructure when TCP/IP is unavailable or unreliable
- Airgapped or occasionally-connected nodes (a field office, a ship, a remote station)
- The surviving UUCP network (active nodes still exist as of 2026)
- Literal sneakernet: serialize spool to removable media, physically carry it, deliver

## stoa-transit: NNTP article batching over UUCP

The batch format is standardized and unchanged since the 1980s.

**Inbound (rnews-compatible intake)**:
- Accept a UUCP batch delivered by `uucico` / `rmail` in `#! rnews` format
- Support uncompressed, `compress`-compressed (`.Z`), and `gzip`-compressed batches
- For each article in the batch: run through the standard stoa ingest pipeline (CID store, group log, duplicate check via message_id map) — identical path to NNTP IHAVE
- Emit metrics: `uucp_batch_articles_received_total`, `uucp_batch_bytes_received_total`

**Outbound (batch sender)**:
- For each configured UUCP peer, maintain a spool of articles queued for that peer
- Pack queued articles into `#! rnews` batches up to a configurable max size (default 500 KB — appropriate for slow links)
- Compress with gzip if the peer advertises support
- Hand batch to `uux <peer>!rnews` for delivery via the local UUCP implementation (`uucico`)
- Configurable send schedule: on-demand (call immediately), batched (accumulate then call), or timed (call at configured intervals — classic dial-up pattern)
- Dedup: do not send an article to a peer that sent it to us (standard ihave/sendme logic)

**Peer config** (in `stoa-smtp` or `stoa-transit` TOML):
```toml
[[uucp.peer]]
name = "neighbor"          # UUCP node name
newsgroups = ["*"]         # groups to exchange (wildmat)
max_batch_bytes = 524288
compression = "gzip"
send_schedule = "batched"  # on-demand | batched | cron
```

## stoa-mail: email transport over UUCP

**Inbound (`rmail` intake)**:
- Provide an `rmail`-compatible binary (or a small shim) that accepts an RFC 5322 message on stdin with UUCP envelope headers and injects it into stoa-mail's SMTP intake path
- Bang path parsing: strip leading `!nodename` hops, resolve final `user@domain` destination
- Handles both old-style bang paths (`!host!user`) and hybrid (`host!user@domain`)

**Outbound (UUCP mail relay)**:
- When the outbound mailer cannot reach a destination via SMTP but a UUCP path is configured, enqueue via `uux <peer>!rmail <recipient>`
- This is a new `UucpMailer` implementing the `OutboundMailer` trait (stoa-y0p2j)
- Routing config: specify which destination domains or bang-path prefixes route via UUCP vs SMTP

## Integration with existing stoa architecture

- UUCP inbound article batches enter the same ingest pipeline as NNTP IHAVE — no special casing in the article store or group log
- UUCP inbound mail enters the same SMTP intake as any other delivery — Delta Chat bridge, sieve filters, JMAP events all fire normally
- `UucpMailer` implements `OutboundMailer` — plugs into `RoutingMailer` with a selector for UUCP-routable destinations
- The UUCP layer does NOT implement its own store — it uses the existing article store and mail store

## What stoa does NOT own

stoa does not implement `uucico`, `uux`, or the UUCP link layer. It relies on a system-installed UUCP implementation (Taylor UUCP, UUCP/GNU, or similar). stoa's job is:
- Producing and consuming `#! rnews` batches
- Providing an `rmail`-compatible intake
- Invoking `uux` to queue outbound jobs
- Configuration to tell the system UUCP which neighbors to call and when

## Acceptance criteria

- Inbound `#! rnews` batch (uncompressed and gzip) correctly ingests all articles into the article store
- Duplicate articles (already seen message_ids) are silently dropped
- Outbound batch for a configured peer contains exactly the articles queued for that peer, in `#! rnews` format
- `rmail` shim accepts a test RFC 5322 message and it appears in the stoa-mail inbox
- Outbound mail to a UUCP-routed domain invokes `uux` with correct arguments
- Integration test using Taylor UUCP in loopback mode: send an article batch to stoa, verify it appears; compose a chat message, verify `uux` invocation

## Design notes

Historical note: the `#! rnews` batch format is documented in the UUCP Project documentation and in the source of INN, C News, and B News. The format is trivial: each article is preceded by a line `#! rnews <byte-count>` and articles are concatenated. Compressed batches wrap the entire concatenation in a single gzip/compress stream preceded by `#! cunbatch` or `#! gunbatch`.
design: stoa is not the UUCP implementation — it is a UUCP-aware application that speaks the batch protocol. Taylor UUCP handles the link layer. This keeps the scope small: batch format parsing/generation and rmail shim are the entire implementation surface.
notes: Review converged after 3 rounds. Final review: stoa-7f5qi. Notable: found and fixed folded-header parsing bug in pipeline.rs via test-driven review.
